newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Bids close on Armenian telecoms tender.
newsitem.headline: Bids close on Armenian telecoms tender.

text.p: Bids in an open tender to sell off 51 percent of Armenia's communications joint venture officialy closed on Friday but the government said it would not reveal the participants or the winner for a month.
The State Tender Committee said it had unsealed the bids for the government's 51 percent share in the Armentel joint venture.

"The participants in the auction will not be announced for one month. During this period the government will negotiate with them and the winner will then be announced," said a statement from the government press office.

Forty-nine percent of Armentel, which handles international communications for the former Soviet republic of three and a half million, is owned by Transworld Telecommunications Inc of the United States.

Observers in Armenia have said that the government wants to take into account security considerations before awarding the tender. The country is in a protracted territorial dispute with neighbouring Azerbaijan.
Some political forces in the country have opposed the sale from the start saying it was not in the interests of the state.

The Armentel sale is part of a big sell-off of large state assets, including the Yerevan Cognac Factory, the Luis electrical lighting equiptment plant, and others. Many are loss-makers and owe millions of dollars in back taxes to the government.
Accelerated privatisation had been a condition of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for further lending to Armenia, which depends on the organisation to help cover a budget deficit.

The government announced on Thursday that it was changing the dates of open tenders of more than 10 major state enterprises including the Cognac plant and Luis. The tenders were postponed by an average of about 1-1/2 months to two months.
The tender for Armentel, however, was brought forward to Friday from the previous planned date of October 15.
No explanation was given for the changes.
Merrill Lynch International is acting as an adviser to the government on the sales.
